answer: At dawn, agents bidding for a delivery from the wharf must each lock a fixed bond in a shared escrow before voting on whether the shipment arrived. A signed receipt anchors the verdict, and a voter who contradicts it forfeits the bond. An attacker creating a crowd of fake agents must therefore lock a separate bond for each one and risks losing those bonds to push a false result. The basalt crates cost no more to count, but the fake votes do.
